name: Pythia
description:
Here is how to read the Pythia config.json. The architecture class is GPTNeoXForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 5,120: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 50,688 × 5,120: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 40, so each head sees 128 dimensions (5,120 / 40). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 5120 / 40 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_hidden_layers is 36: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 20,480. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 5,120-wide stream is projected up, activated with gelu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 2,048 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is.

vocab_size is 50,688. 50,688 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is false, so the input embedding matrix and the output LM head are separate learned matrices rather than a shared transpose.

torch_dtype is float16.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/EleutherAI/pythia-12b/blob/main/config.json.
